messages:
mira: heads-up — saw p99.9 spikes on the console mux this morning, correlating with RBAC cache misses for a handful of tenants. p99.9 jumped ~420ms -> ~1.5s between 08:10-08:14. logs: authz:cache-miss=421k, authz:latency-p99=820ms. anyone else seeing this?
sam: saw the same. looks like a burst of dashboard renders from a customer that triggered thousands of distinct subject lookups. authz service got thrashed, downstream mux queueing.
andrew: quick idea — add a lightweight rate-shaper in the mux before we invoke per-request authz. per-tenant token-bucket + a global smoothing budget to flatten spikes. when cache-miss rate crosses threshold, slow-path authz calls get queued and we priming authz cache in the background.
jia: queued authz worries me re: revocations. if permissions were just revoked, queuing could allow stale access for a bit. how long of a window are we okay with being eventually consistent?
mira: valid. proposal: keep shaping window tiny (~1-2s) for smoothing; if a permission_revocation_marker exists for a subject we bypass shaping and force immediate fresh check. also add an opt-in stricter mode for sensitive dashboards (no shaping).
sam: + metrics to track: mux p99/p999 pre/post, authz cache hit-rate, number of shaped requests, and revocation-bypass counts. Also add a circuit-breaker path: if authz service is overloaded, fall back to a read-only projection (panels that can show non-sensitive data) instead of full render.
andrew: implementation sketch: 1) RFC describing mux-rate-shaper interface and config knobs (per-tenant QPS, bucket refill, global budget) 2) PoC behind feature-flag for two high-concurrency tenants 3) synthetic loadtests that exercise permission churn and measure p999 4) gradual canary + rollout. rough timeline: 3 sprints to stable.
jia: +1 on RFC and PoC. also request we add audit-log tagging whenever we serve using cached authz vs fresh eval — important for security reviews.
mira: sounds good. I'll start the RFC draft and attach perf dashboards. TL;DR: add per-tenant token-bucket shaper, authz priming, revocation-bypass marker, and fallback projection. @eng-oncall-bot please watch mux p99.9 and authz:cache-miss after the flag flips. :thumbsup:
